Hi Devraccoon! No, AI hasn’t been used to help me cowrite the description. However, Google Translate has been used to translate some words. As mentioned in the “Includes AI Generated Content”: AI was only used to generate the mod image and some general troubleshooting.

I used to work at a company where I created loads of documentation and sent countless e-mails to customers and other companies so I guess that writing style stuck with me. I might be physically incapable of writing “yeah, this mod adds overpowered ammo” without making it sound like documentation.

If you’re curious, this is how I normally work when writing:

  1. Write it in my original language.
  2. Reread it a couple of times to catch errors.
  3. Rewrite in English.
  4. Reread again.

comments.author: neverwinternightshift
comments.body_html:
I noticed that the initial speed for every round was too high, resulting in having to aim down when using a scope, as the round was zeroed at a considerable range. I ended up adding a line:

“BallisticCoeficient”: 0.995,

I also removed the lines for initial speed. This means the round flies at stock speed, but with very little drop over great distances. In turn, the scopes are more accurate. I was able to shoot the sniper sitting atop the pipe system on Customs from Streamer House with almost no drop.

Unsure if this is desired, but it does make the rounds a lot more stable.

On a side note, I added a background color of red to the lines by adding:

“BackgroundColor”: “red”,

comments.author: said02
comments.body_html: Hi. Could you say how to add these lines in what file?

comments.author: neverwinternightshift
comments.body_html:
Head into the mod folder for hyperlethal. You’ll want Hyperlethal > db > items. Each round has its own folder. Inside is a JSON you can open with any text editor. You’ll have to change each one for the rounds you’re wanting to edit. The lines you’re wanting to change are:

Remove: “InitialSpeed”: xxxxx

Add: “BallisticCoeficient”: 0.995, (That’s not a typo, they use 1 f in Coeficient in the main SPT files)

Add (Optional): “BackgroundColor”: “red”,

I added the Ballistic Coefficient line in alphabetical order for the override lines in each round’s JSON file, hence the comma at the end of the line. Same for BackgroundColor. If you place them at the end, you’ll want to add a comma to the last entry that’s already there, then leave a comma off the last one, so it’s a complete list. After that you can test fire, but it should be a lot closure to true aim.

comments.author: neverwinternightshift
comments.body_html:
To change Mechanic’s selling price for HL rounds, I edited the mechanic_assort.json file, located in the assorts folder. Within the file, you’ll find the ID entry for (as an example) 9x19 Hyper Lethal. You can find the IDs for each item in their respective item json files, located in the items folder.

Note that the tpl (template ID) is the actual item ID for 9x19 Hyper Lethal. Above it is an ID that is referenced further down. Search it, and further down you’ll find an entry that looks like this.

Change the count to whatever you want Mechanic to charge (it’s set at 1500 in this example).

––>Restart your server.<––

If you want to change the handbook and flea prices, you can find them in the individual database json files for each item. Locate these entries in each item json file:

“fleaPriceRoubles”
“handbookPriceRoubles”

Change to the desired price. I hope this helps.

comments.author: neverwinternightshift
comments.body_html:
If you want, you can always add recoil values to each ammo as desired. Head into the items folder and find the json file for each ammo type. In the “overrideProperties” section, simply add:

“Recoil”: 0, <— Note the comma. If you add it at the end of the section, it won’t need that. You need to add it to the line above. Otherwise, you can just paste that entry between any two lines in the section and it’ll add the override to that round, overriding the default template values.

Change the 0 to any value you like. If you want to reduce recoil, make the value negative. -10 means 10% less recoil. 10 means 10% more.

comments.author: neverwinternightshift
comments.body_html:
I’ve tweaked it quite a bit myself. The first tweak I did was to head to the creator’s github and reference the table he has for round IDs so I could start adding the missing HL rounds. The only one not present in his table (that I wanted) was 5.7x28mm rounds (for the P90 and 5-7 Pistol). This means there’s no existing ID, so I assigned it one. 6600000000000000000000009, an ID which is not used by the other rounds in the table.

Here’s an example of the 5.7x28mm round I created. Each comment notes something I changed and why. To create the base file, I just copied the folder for 9x19 in the items folder and renamed it and its file to reflect 57x28.

I also made sure I added these new rounds to Mechanic so I could buy them. Should you do that as well, you can add them to mechanic using SVM. Head to the Advanced Features section, specifically “Create a new trader offer”. Add the item.

Hope this is helpful for future tweaks.
